summary:
Fine-stage similarity landscape around T at 0.3 mm (oct150 pooled x2, mri pooled x4), inside a specimen mask = (MRI tissue eroded 1.3 mm, mapped through T) & oct150_mask = 7.97 cm3 (old mask 28.6 cm3), intersected at every pose with the moving MRI tissue mask ("overlap" mask; a "fixed" mask variant agrees within +-2 mm).

Main result: the OCT(mu_s) <-> MRI intensity relation at this scale is INVERTED. Raw masked NCC at T is -0.23, flattened (sigma 3 mm) NCC -0.13, LCC(w=9) -0.10, and all three are sharp V-shaped MINIMA at T along all 6 axes; i.e. |NCC| peaks at T. Regionally, 70% of ~7 mm sub-blocks (26/37) and 7/8 half-blocks are negative (volume-weighted mean -0.15, range -0.63..+0.18), so a global polarity flip is justified but not universal. This explains the structural stage's negative "WM channel" and the near-zero (+0.03) raw NCC: the sign was wrong, not the signal.

Ranking by peak-to-shoulder contrast (sign-corrected, overlap mask, higher = better): -NCC flat sigma 3 mm 0.54 (value 0.130 at T) > -LCC w=9/15/21 0.45/0.45/0.43 (0.098/0.137/0.155) > -NCC flat sigma 6 0.42 (0.187) > -NCC raw 0.36 (0.230) > LCC^2 (sign-free) 0.21-0.31 > MI-32 0.28 (0.072) ~ in-plane |grad| NCC 0.29 (0.18; peak biased 1.6 mm in y, ragged surface) > NGF 0.09-0.11 > MIND-SSC 0.02 (no optimum at all at 0.3 mm; monotonic drift). Half-widths of the winners: 1.2-3 mm in translation, 4-8 deg in rotation (rotations about the block centre move the 28 mm mask edge only ~2.4 mm at 10 deg, hence flat).

Is T the optimum? Within one to three 0.3 mm voxels. Parabolic peak offsets agree across all 11 measures on the DIRECTION: OCT-y axis -0.25..-0.94 mm (all negative; intensity measures -0.55..-0.94), OCT-x axis +0.05..+1.0 mm (all positive), depth ~0 (+-0.5, mixed sign). 2-D maps (1 mm grid) put the -NCC argmax at (depth 0, y -1) and (depth 0, x +1), LCC^2 at (depth +1, 0), MI exactly at T. Rotations: intensity measures say +1.7..+2.5 deg about OCT-x, MI and |grad| say -3 deg -> undetermined at the +-3 deg level; about depth/y no consensus (|offset| <= 4 deg with flat profiles). So T is essentially right at 0.3 mm and the fine stage is a sub-mm polish.

Wall time (CPU, 4 threads, 1.37 M voxels): resample 0.15-0.18 s; NCC 0.007 s; MI 0.01-0.02 s; separable LCC w9/15/21 0.26/0.40/0.51 s (naive avg_pool3d 9^3: 4.0 s); NGF 0.44 s; MIND 0.37+0.04 s; |grad| prep 0.34 s. Autograd fwd+bwd w.r.t. rigid params: -NCC flat (point-based, Refiner-style) 0.23 s, in-plane |grad| NCC 0.57 s, LCC^2 w15 1.21 s; histogram MI is not differentiable.

Recommendation: polarity-flipped masked NCC of 3 mm-bias-flattened intensities as the fine-stage loss (cheapest, sharpest, differentiable via the existing Refiner path with a sign change), with -LCC (4.5 mm box) as the local/verification variant and MI-32 as the sign-free QC; drop MIND/NGF/|grad| at this scale; guard the sign per level with the sub-block polarity test.
recipe:
RECOMMENDED FINE-STAGE SIMILARITY ("negNCC_flat3"), exact definition:
1. Grids. Level 1: OCT = oct150 avg-pooled x2 (0.30 mm, shape 97x133x106, affine via octreg.common.avg_pool_iso); MRI = mri.npy avg-pooled x4 (0.32 mm, 85x122x123). Level 2: oct150 (0.15 mm) and mri pooled x2 (0.16 mm). OCT is the fixed image; MRI is sampled at transformed OCT points (T = OCT world -> MRI world, as in Refiner.loss_of).
2. Bias flattening (pose independent, done once per level in each image's own space, masked normalised convolution): F = I / ( G_sigma*(I*m) / (G_sigma*m + 1e-6) + 1e-3*mean(I[m]) ), sigma = 3.0 mm Gaussian (kernel radius 3 sigma, zero padding). OCT: m = specimen mask m_spec. MRI: m = mri_tissue pooled (>0.5).
3. Masks. m_spec = ( resample_to_grid(erode_ball(mri_tissue_pooled>0.5, r=1.3 mm), A_mri_p, A_oct_p, shape, T_grid_to_vol=T0) > 0.5 ) & (oct150_mask pooled > 0.5), with T0 = the pose at the start of the level (recompute m_spec when the level changes; keep it fixed inside a level). Evaluation mask at pose T: m(T) = m_spec & ( mri_tissue_pooled sampled through T > 0.5 ) (the moving-tissue intersection is treated as a constant, no gradient).
4. Loss to MINIMISE: L(T) = + NCC_m(F_oct, F_mri o T)   [i.e. maximise the NEGATIVE correlation; equivalently feed -F_mri to the existing masked_ncc and minimise 1 - NCC]. NCC_m = sum_m (a-mean_m a)(b-mean_m b) / sqrt(sum_m (a-mean)^2 sum_m (b-mean)^2), trilinear grid_sample for F_mri at OCT mask voxel centres (Refiner.loss_of with FM = F_mri[None], FO = F_oct[None], oct_mask = m_spec; only the sign flips). Cost 0.23 s fwd+bwd at 0.3 mm on 4 CPU threads; Adam on (rotvec, t) exactly as Refiner.refine; dof rigid first, then similarity/affine with the existing ls/sh clamps.
5. Local variant for verification / second level: -LCC_w(F_oct_z, F_mri_z o T) with a separable box window w = 4.5 mm (15 vox at 0.3 mm; 29 vox at 0.15 mm), masked local statistics n=box(m), mu=box(x m)/n, var=box(x^2 m)/n - mu^2, cov=box(a b m)/n - mu_a mu_b, LCC = cov / sqrt(var_a var_b + 1e-2) on globally z-scored inputs, averaged over voxels with m & n>0.5. Implement box as three avg_pool3d passes with kernels (w,1,1),(1,w,1),(1,1,w), stride 1, padding w//2, count_include_pad=True (0.40 s fwd, 1.2 s fwd+bwd at 0.3 mm; the naive w^3 avg_pool3d is 10-15x slower). Value 0.137 at T, contrast 0.45, peak offsets <= 0.9 mm / 1.7 deg.
6. Polarity guard (run at the start of every level at the current pose): raw masked NCC in a 4x4x4 sub-block tiling of the mask bounding box (blocks with > 2000 voxels); flip the sign (use step 4) only if >= 65% of blocks are negative AND the volume-weighted mean is negative (here 26/37 = 70%, mean -0.15). If the sign is mixed, use the sign-free LCC^2 (= cov^2/(var_a var_b + 1e-2), same window; contrast 0.25-0.31 here, peak +0.6..0.9 mm in depth) instead.
7. QC after convergence: MI (32 bins, joint histogram, bin ranges = 0.5-99.5 percentiles of raw OCT / raw resampled MRI inside the mask, fixed at the start pose) must be within 0.001 of its 1-D peak (its peak was within 0.33 mm / 3 deg of T here; contrast 0.28); and the sampled 1-D profiles of L along the 3 OCT axes (+-0.5, 1, 2 mm; +-1, 2, 5 deg about the block centre) must be unimodal with maximum at the final pose.
Do not use at 0.3 mm: MIND-SSC (contrast 0.02, no optimum), NGF (0.09-0.11), |grad| NCC (peak biased 1.5-2 mm in y and -4 deg about y; stripe sensitive: in-plane variant 0.18 vs full 0.09 at T). Perturbations for landscape checks: T' = T @ P, P a translation along the OCT array axes (world unit vectors A_oct[:,k]/|.|: depth = world +z, y = world -y, x = world +x) or a rotation about those axes through the OCT block centre c_o = A_oct @ [(shape-1)/2, 1] = (15.89, -20.02, 14.54) mm.

caveats:
1. Polarity: the dominant OCT(mu_s) <-> MRI relation at 0.3 mm is INVERSE (raw NCC -0.23 at T), contradicting the brief's note that MRI shows the tracts bright; it is consistent with the pipeline argument mri_wm_bright=False and with the negative WM-channel NCC of the structural stage. It is not universal: ~30% of ~7 mm sub-blocks correlate positively (up to +0.18), so a global sign flip is a compromise; re-run the sub-block polarity test at each finer level (0.15 / 0.04 mm fibre texture may correlate with the opposite sign) and fall back to sign-free LCC^2 where the sign is mixed.
2. Circularity: T was produced by an NCC-type optimiser on class maps derived from the same intensities, so NCC-like measures peaking at T is partly expected. The independent measures (MI, NGF, |grad|) also put the optimum within ~1 mm / ~3 deg, but with lower contrast; the rotation offsets from the flat-profile measures (NGF/|grad| about y: -4 deg) are not trustworthy.
3. The specimen mask is derived from T itself (eroded 1.3 mm MRI tissue mapped through T); it is valid only while the pose error is below ~1.3 mm, which the landscapes indicate. The fixed-mask variant exaggerates the shoulders beyond +-2 mm through the MRI air boundary; within +-2 mm both masks agree.
4. Rotation profiles are intrinsically flat: a 10 deg rotation about the block centre moves the 28 mm mask edge only ~2.4 mm; the reported contrast is therefore dominated by the translation shoulders, and rotational offsets are undetermined at the +-3 deg level.
5. Only 1-D and two 2-D translation slices were sampled (no full 6-D search); local optimum tests at +-0.5 mm / +-1 deg are at the level of trilinear-interpolation noise for the smoother measures.
6. MIND-SSC and NGF being useless here is a 0.3 mm statement (OCT interior is smooth at this scale); they may become informative at 0.04-0.15 mm where fibre texture appears.
7. Bias flattening sigma: 1.3 mm sigma (3 mm FWHM) removes most of the signal (|NCC| 0.05); 3 mm sigma keeps it (0.13) with the highest relative contrast; 6 mm / raw keep more absolute correlation (0.19 / 0.23) but a lower contrast and a rot-z bias of -4 deg -> use sigma = 3 mm.
8. Timings are CPU (4 threads); the autograd timing print omitted the gradient values (grads were reset before printing), but backward executed and the loss values match the forward evaluations. The naive LCC in sweep 1 (avg_pool3d w^3) is 10-15x slower than the separable implementation used in the follow-up; use the separable form.
9. The MI landscape is the cleanest sign-free check (peak within 0.33 mm / 3 deg of T) but histogram MI is not differentiable; a Parzen-window MI would cost more than the recommended NCC loss and was not timed.
